Name: Heinrich Bullinger
Summary: Swiss reformer (1504-1575) who succeeded Zwingli in Zurich and became the most widely consulted Reformed leader of his generation.
Contribution: He held Zurich steady for over forty years, corresponded with reformers and rulers across Europe, and wrote the Second Helvetic Confession, which became a standard statement of Reformed faith in Switzerland and beyond.
Testimony: His long, steady pastorate in Zurich made the city a refuge and a centre of counsel for Reformed churches abroad.
